content.title: How To Become a Mortgage Loan Officer (With Salary)
content.text: Finding a jobHow To Become a Mortgage Loan Officer (With Salary)Written byUpdated December 10, 2025How to become a mortgage loan officerResponsibilities of a mortgage loan officerSkills for a mortgage loan officerSalary and job outlook for a mortgage loan officerA mortgage loan officer helps clients determine whether they qualify for home loans. They also provide information on the types of loans available and interest rates. This can be a rewarding career if you're interested in real estate and like working with a variety of people. In this article, we discuss how to become a mortgage loan officer, and we offer information about the average salary and job outlook for this role.How to become a mortgage loan officerHere are the steps you can follow to become a mortgage loan officer:1. Meet the basic requirementsTo become a mortgage loan officer, you need to be at least 18 years old and have a high school diploma or GED. While in school, try to take math- and finance-based classes to start gaining some knowledge and skills needed to for this role.2. Complete pre-licensure coursesThe National Mortgage Licensing Service (NMLS) requires mortgage loan officers to take certain pre-licensure courses to ensure they thoroughly understand what this career entails. These courses cover topics like:Federal law and regulationsEthics, including sections about fraud, fair lending and consumer protection issuesTraining related to lending standards in the non-traditional mortgage product marketAdditional instruction on mortgage originationRequired education also includes courses on mortgage lending laws in your state and other state-specific topics. Learn more about the state-by-state education requirements by visiting the NMLS website.3. Research your state's licensure requirementsOnce you complete your pre-licensure courses, your next step toward becoming a mortgage loan officer involves getting a valid mortgage origination license. State agencies issue these licenses, and each state has its own guidelines for obtaining licensure. You also need to pay fees to receive licensure, which varies by state.4. Pass the SAFE MLO testThe Secure and Fair Enforcement for Mortgage Licensing Act (SAFE) resulted in the creation of a national registry and licensing process for mortgage loan professionals. To receive your license, you must first meet certain requirements, and then you need to pass an exam that measures your knowledge of both federal and state mortgage lending laws. 5. Fulfill NMLS requirementsMortgage loan professionals are required to register with the Nationwide Mortgage Licensing System and Registry (NMLS) and pass certain qualifications and background checks.Other NMLS requirements you need include:Sponsorship: Ensure that your employer sponsors and supervises your duties. Your state's regulatory body also must approve your sponsorships.NMLS Unique Identifier: This is a permanent number that every professional, real estate company and branch with an NMLS account has. These unique Identifiers help track companies and licensees and are listed on all advertisements for mortgage origination services.6. Maintain active licensureAfter you get your license, you need to keep it active by meeting certain requirements, like keeping your information up to date. For example, if you begin working for a new company, you must notify the NMLS of this change to update your unique identifier. You can visit the NMLS website to learn more about deadlines, fees, checklists, license renewal and updating your mortgage loan officer information.7. Continue your educationMortgage loan officers must complete eight hours of NMLS-approved continuing coursework each year to be eligible for license renewal. This education must include:Three hours of regulations and federal lawTwo hours of ethics coursework on fraud, fair lending and consumer protectionTwo hours of training on lending standards for the non-traditional mortgage product marketOne hour on mortgage origination services, which you can complete by taking a state-specific course8. Gain experienceOnce you have fulfilled all education and licensure requirements, get experience working as a mortgage loan officer. You can work independently, although you may want to seek employment at an established mortgage lending company, bank or credit union for your first job.Related: 17 Types of Real Estate Jobs To ExploreResponsibilities of a mortgage loan officerThe primary responsibilities of a mortgage loan officer include:Collect all borrowers' financial information, including taxes and debt, for the loanPresent clients with loan options that are a good fit for themIdentify future homebuyers through advertising, seminars and other channelsMaintain detailed and factually correct documents on mortgage transactionsCoordinate with other real estate professionals, like home appraisers and underwritersComply with confidentiality policies and privacy laws throughout the mortgage application processRelated: Loan Officer vs. Real Estate Agent: What's the Difference?Skills for a mortgage loan officerTo be a successful mortgage loan officer, consider developing these skills:Interpersonal skillsMortgage loan officers explain different loan options to borrowers in simple terms, keep clients updated with their loan status and refer them to helpful resources. Interpersonal skills can help them connect with borrowers and make the loan process smoother.OrganizationMortgage loan officers often work on multiple loans at the same time, making organization an important skill to develop. It also helps them keep track of their continuing education and licensing requirements.Attention to detailSince mortgage loan officers work with a lot of numbers and specific loan factors, attention to detail is particularly useful. With this skill, they can ensure interest rates, loan amounts and borrower information are correct.Financial skillsMortgage loan officers should have detailed financial knowledge to help borrowers make informed decisions. They spend most of their days reviewing finances, including credit scores and income, to determine whether borrowers qualify for different loans.Salary and job outlook for a mortgage loan officerThe national average salary for a loan officer is $186,191 per year. Many factors can influence salary, including location, employer and years of experience. For the most up-to-date salary information from Indeed, click on the links provided.According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, the employment of loan officers is projected to grow by 2% between 2024 and 2034, which is slower than the average across all occupations.Please note that, at the time of this article's writing, the companies, institutions or organizations mentioned in this article may or may not be affiliated with Indeed, and their mention in this article does not imply a business relationship with Indeed. The information on this site is provided as a courtesy and for informational purposes only.
